England's latest blueprint of attack: Thomas Tuchel has switched style since World Cup but clunky win over Croatia showed growing pains - Spain will put it to severe test, writes JACK GAUGHAN

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:17 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • It was gone 11pm when Thomas Tuchel was shaking the hands of Harry Kane’s parents on the Wembley pitch while the children of England’s record appearance maker enjoyed the run of the national stadium in front of 90,000 empty seats.
  • This was time for Kane to fully take in the emotion of an historic night alongside his family and that Tuchel was out there too felt instructive of their relationship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:17 EST, 13 November 2026.

It was gone 11pm when Thomas Tuchel was shaking the hands of Harry Kane’s parents on the Wembley pitch while the children of England’s record appearance maker enjoyed the run of the national stadium in front of 90,000 empty seats.

This was time for Kane to fully take in the emotion of an historic night alongside his family and that Tuchel was out there too felt instructive of their relationship.

Kane and Tuchel had frank conversations last month about the World Cup fallout, on how England might be best tinkering with their selection when chasing games.

The manager respects and values his captain’s opinion on these things, recognising that he is almost completely agenda-free, as they attempt to better plot a route to silverware in readiness for the European Championship in 18 months’ time.

If there was uncertainty about identity and style when the World Cup crunch arrived, when Enzo Fernandez was pulling stupid faces and the colour drained from England faces, then players have felt that the detail on how Tuchel wants to move forward has been clear across the first two camps since America.

Thursday night was not vintage against a Croatia team they battered 7-0 a few weeks back. Tuchel and Kane both admitted that afterwards but it is noticeable that there is a defined plan on how they intend to attack in a slightly different way.

Thomas Tuchel embraces Harry Kane's wife Katie at Wembley on Thursday night.

Harry Kane (centre) and Co are changing the way they attack after the World Cup.

Were Tuchel to have been able to pick a first-choice back four then the win would likely have been more comfortable, Croatia benefiting from individual errors. And a lack of cutting edge inside the box hindered the hosts too.

The idea behind what they were doing appeared well thought out though and that should bring about some gentle encouragement.

The full backs, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall, were both consistently worked into hugely dangerous areas in the inside channels, while the make-up of Tuchel’s midfield felt very deliberate as well.

Sources indicate that it is no coincidence that England enjoyed the highest amount of possession in the half spaces ten yards inside Croatia’s half. That is a clear directive, with both Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice drifting wider to create overloads and the full backs pushed into threatening spaces.

Sources indicate that ‘Declan understands the game like he’s almost a coach on the field and in a perfect position to manage all these things from behind,’ Tuchel noted this week. To have a constant interchanging unit, he does need brains.

These are the rotations that the Three Lions didn’t engineer enough of over in the United States, with Kane dropping deep as he does and completing that wonder crossfield pass for the Morgan Rogers opener.

They are the moments that Tuchel is preaching, Jude Bellingham taking up an unusual position in order to stretch Croatia as he squared for the Chelsea forward.

What Tuchel needs now is to work on how that can be translated into making sure his very best players can affect matches more regularly inside the opponent’s box.

Jude Bellingham only touched the ball four times in Croatia's box in the 2-1 win.

England manager Thomas Tuchel will speak to his players about what to do if racial abuse mars Sunday’s Nations League group decider against Spain in Madrid.

The England team have been on the wrong end of racism in Madrid before – back in 2004 – and refused to play a friendly there in 2008, insisting the fixture be moved to Seville.

In March this year, meanwhile, Spanish fans chanted anti-Muslim songs during a game with Egypt in Barcelona and the World champions have been subsequently ordered by FIFA to play their next friendly in a partially-closed stadium.

Recent findings suggest that there will be a full house at Athletico Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano stadium as England try to topple Spain from the top of their group on Sunday and Tuchel stated: ‘I think I hear about it [the Barcelona incident] for the first time that this happens. I think it's unacceptable.

‘In any stadium we will never accept racism.

Industry observers note that ‘I expect full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything else. And I think the referee in the games and the officials know about that.

According to recent reports, ‘I think we had a same discussion before the Serbia game [last year]. There is a protocol in place.

‘Yeah, maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Spain].’.

Tuchel and the FA expect a hostile atmosphere in Madrid, especially as two Real players – Jude Bellingham and Trent Alexander-Arnold - will be in the England squad.

Last year’s Serbia game passed without incident in Belgrade and the FA are confident the same will apply this weekend.

Recent findings suggest that seven years ago in Sofia, though, captain Harry Kane almost led the England team off the field after following FIFA protocols by alerting the referee to abuse aimed at Tyrone Mings, Raheem Sterling and Marcus Rashford. The game was paused while the culprits were thrown out.

‘I still think the protocol is in place and it's important that the players know about is,’ added Tuchel.

‘And then yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. The best answers are on the pitch.’.

The FIFA protocol – adopted by UEFA and the Premier League – is a four step-process that starts with a player alerting match officials and is followed by a warning to the crowd, a possible suspension of play and, if necessary, the abandonment of the game.

That Kane only touched it six times inside the 18-yard area and Bellingham on just four occasions points to a team still figuring themselves out.

Sources indicate that that will be put to the severe test in Madrid on Sunday. England do not beat the truly elite nations; never have.

And it’ll be interesting to see whether Tuchel sticks to this sort of plan, one designed to dominate, or if he instead relies on the counter-attacking ability of a group he has viewed as a ‘Premier League team’ before now, leaning into their physicality.

If England are feeling confident enough, giving this tweaked style a go against the world champions might offer them some answers on what could be achieved when the proper silverware is on the line.

Breaking: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4808 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • Sources indicate that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

Sources indicate that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he mentioned.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Recent findings suggest that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

It has been revealed that that was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a new manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Recent findings suggest that playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Sources indicate that millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil remarked: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

“We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

The draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

The third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” stated Willock after the match.

It has been revealed that “100% [the competition is key], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a massive game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We said at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Recent findings suggest that marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Sources indicate that issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Sources indicate that double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Industry observers note that free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

It has been revealed that millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

According to recent reports, the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

Recent findings suggest that the delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

According to recent reports, millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Sources indicate that hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Sources indicate that barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

In a recent development, wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

It has been revealed that newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

It has been revealed that murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

Sources indicate that the teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

According to recent reports, alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach states has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

In a recent development, at the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

In a recent development, bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

In a recent development, aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight latest signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London.

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

We’re bringing you the action from the pick of tonight’s EFL Cup games but there are also four games kicking off at 7.45pm:.

Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

The Champions League also returns tonight and you can follow along with both our blogs:.

Aston Villa are currently 3-1 up against Club Brugge in Belgium – follow the action here.

Manchester City will face Porto at 8.00pm – our live blog has just gone live here with the team news from both sides.

Here is how the visitors are lining up:.

Yoane Wissa takes the captain’s armband tonight, while Jacob Ramsey starts up front after scoring a late equaliser against Bournemouth on Saturday.

Your Mags at Millwall ✊ pic.twitter.com/zfnHgTlWgh.

Here is your Millwall starting XI:.

Keeper Filip Marschall is making his debut while Jensen Metcalfe is back in the squad after his red card against Bolton was overturned on appeal.

How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the upcoming season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

Archiviata la sosta per le Nazionali, tornano i vari campionati: l'Inter è attesa dalla trasferta sul campo dell'Atalanta. L'ex centrocampista Christian Brocchi ne ha parlato a sitiscommesse.com: "Con l'Italia Pio Esposito ha segnato 10 gol in 15 partite e sta dimostrando a tutti di poter essere il centravanti della Nazionale per i prossimi dieci anni. Segna tantissimo perché è il terminale offensivo di una Nazionale che si sta costruendo, che è in crescita e che gli dà la possibilità di mettere in risalto le sue qualità: quelle della punta centrale, dell'attaccante d'area di rigore, che però quando esce sa anche giocare con la squadra. I suoi numeri in Nazionale sono impressionanti, visto che ha superato gente come Vieri e Toni, che avevano fatto qualcosa di straordinario. Il ritorno all'Inter sarà dolce: rientra più forte di quando è partito prima della sosta, perché i gol segnati in azzurro avranno fatto crescere ancora di più la consapevolezza di essere un giocatore importante. Chivu, che non aveva certo bisogno di questo, sa che i due titolari sono Lautaro e Marcus Thuram, ma sa anche benissimo che Pio è un titolare allo stesso modo e che, se manca uno dei due, è il giocatore più importante che ha a disposizione".

Industry observers note that "Dalla Nazionale sono tornati anche Barella e Bastoni, che hanno giocato 180 minuti in quattro giorni, ma per me devono giocare sempre: sono due colonne portanti, i giocatori sui quali l'Inter ha costruito i propri successi negli ultimi anni. Ci può stare che in alcune partite non riescano a reggere l'urto fisico e atletico, perché giocano davvero tanto, ma sono troppo importanti nello scacchiere nerazzurro e io li metterei sempre in campo".

In a recent development, "Quanto alla squadra, dopo il derby perso Chivu l'ha abbassata di qualche metro e ha rimodulato il pressing, e nella partita con il Como l'Inter non ha preso gol. La questione non è abbassarsi un po' oppure no, ma capire il momento: in quella fase l'Inter aveva bisogno di sentirsi più solida e ha cambiato qualcosa dal punto di vista tattico, ma nelle partite successive potrebbe rialzarsi e riproporsi in maniera diversa. Dopo il derby l'obiettivo numero uno era riprendere il passo, e io resto della mia idea: l'Inter è la squadra più forte e la più accreditata per la vittoria dello scudetto".

Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Alle soddisfazioni della sosta si affianca ora la gestione delle energie. In vista del Lecce, Gattuso ragiona su turnover e modulo.

Industry observers note that provstgaard e Isaksen hanno giocato entrambi tutti i 99 minuti con la Danimarca. Il difensore ha retto l’urto, mentre Isaksen ha servito un assist. In Nations League, però, i danesi si sono fatti rimontare dalla Norvegia.

Come osserva Il Messaggero, a Formello le presenze nelle selezioni sono motivo d’orgoglio. I calciatori biancocelesti hanno ritrovato spazio e attenzione: alle convocazioni sono seguite le titolarità e, nel caso di Isaksen, anche un assist.

Per il club è una soddisfazione legata al riconoscimento sul campo dei propri giocatori, dopo un periodo in cui il loro valore di mercato era stato spesso al centro dell’attenzione. Il rovescio riguarda il rientro: le nazionali restituiscono i calciatori alla Lazio proprio mentre riprendono gli impegni. È in questo quadro che Gattuso valuta le scelte per il Lecce.

It has been revealed that L'Udinese cerca soluzioni per uscire da un momento complicato della stagione, con la classifica che impone una reazione e un reparto offensivo che fatica a trovare continuità. Nicolò Zaniolo non è ancora riuscito a garantire un rendimento costante, mentre Keinan Davis è ancora alla ricerca del primo gol in campionato. Il rientro di Vakoun Bayo rappresenta una risorsa aggiuntiva per lo staff tecnico, ma pesa soprattutto l'assenza di Idrissa Gueye, giovane attaccante senegalese che si era messo in evidenza prima di fermarsi per un grave infortunio alla caviglia. Il suo recupero procede e arrivano segnali incoraggianti.

In a recent development, gueye si è infortunato lo scorso 5 ottobre durante l'amichevole disputata in Polonia contro il Pogon Stettino. Il problema alla caviglia ha reso necessario un intervento chirurgico, seguito da un percorso riabilitativo che dovrebbe permettergli di tornare a disposizione a gennaio. A circa un mese e mezzo dall'incidente, l'attaccante ha compiuto un passo importante: come riporta il portale TuttoUdinese.it, è tornato a camminare e ha ripreso a lavorare in palestra, concentrandosi sul recupero della condizione fisica. Un progresso significativo, anche se il ritorno agli allenamenti sul campo dovrà attendere il completamento delle diverse tappe previste dal programma medico.

Il suo rientro potrebbe rappresentare una sorta di nuovo acquisto per l'Udinese, soprattutto considerando i margini di crescita del giovane centravanti. La società potrebbe comunque intervenire sul mercato di gennaio per rinforzare il reparto offensivo e offrire maggiori alternative a Paolo Zanetti. Ritrovare Gueye, però, sarebbe già un'iniezione di fiducia per una squadra che ha bisogno di aumentare la propria pericolosità sotto porta. L'obiettivo è recuperarlo al meglio, senza forzare i tempi, per metterlo nelle condizioni di dare un contributo nella seconda parte della stagione.

Industry News: Conte: “Penso che prima o poi il cerchio con la Juventus si dovrà chiudere”

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (443 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Iamnaples

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

“Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio. “So di aver lasciato qualcosa e quel cerchio lo dobbiamo chiudere. In passato ci sono stati momenti in cui avremmo potuto ritrovarci, ma è molto difficile, perché devono verificarsi due condizioni: io devo essere libero e la Juventus deve essere alla ricerca di un allenatore. Ci sono state due occasioni concrete. La prima quando la Juventus scelse Maurizio Sarri: io ero senza squadra e, alla fine, andai all’Inter. La seconda quando arrivò Giuntoli, che decise di puntare su Thiago Motta: in quel caso io finii al Napoli. Dopo Bari potevo diventare l’allenatore della Juventus, avevo parlato più volte con Castagnini e con Secco, c’era Ranieri in panchina, poi presero Ferrara per fare le ultime partite per andare in Champions. Loro sapevano benissimo che avrei fatto il 4-2-4, avendo attaccanti come Amauri, Iaquinta, Treseguet e Del Piero, dissi “con gli attaccanti siamo a posto, dobbiamo prendere degli esterni”. Loro, non so per quale motivo, presero Diego dal Werder Brema e mi chiamarono per avere delle rassicurazioni. Io vado, entro da allenatore della Juve e mi chiedono come volessi giocare e io dico “ancora? con il 4-2-4”. Mi chiesero dovre avrei messo Diego e io dissi “lo avete comprato, anche se abbiamo 4 attaccanti, lo metto al fianco alla punta”. Mi sento dire “Diego vuole giocare con il 4-3-1-2” e in quel momento pensa alla mia follia che fa capire che sono una persona dritta che non scende a compromessi. Un altro avrebbe detto “te lo faccio giocare anche in porta, basta che mi fai questo contratto”. Io forte delle mie idee e delle mie convinzioni, perchè non voglio scendere a compromessi, gli dico “se il giocatore deve decidere come giocare, non sono io l’allenatore giusto per voi”. Vado via da li ed esco che non sono più l’allenatore della Juventus”.

Published: 17:03 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 13 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino already has a fresh injury headache at Manchester United - and he's not even through the door yet.

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home from Denmark duty having failed a series of physical tests.

The full-back missed four Premier League matches in October due to a hamstring injury but came on to provide an assist and score the equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Now he re-joins an injury list which includes Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Carlos Baleba, and potentially Harry Maguire, with Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko ruled out longer-term.

Denmark's team doctor Martin Boesen said: 'We have carried out a series of tests on Dorgu, and he has not performed well enough to be ready to play in the two matches.

'He needs further recovery time after his injury, so we are sending him home for additional rehabilitation.'.

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home fromDenmark duty after failing a series of fitness tests.

It is potentially another thing for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino to worry about.

Dorgu, 22, will miss matches against Portugal and Norway in the Nations League.

Pochettino will hope Dorgu makes a quick recovery as he seeks to get Manchester United back on track.

United, who sit 18th in the Premier League, agreed to pay more than £10million to prise Pochettino and his staff away from the United States national team.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick and will get down to business after his final matches in charge of the USA against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

The former Southampton, Tottenham, and Chelsea boss broke down in tears as he began his farewell and admitted that he couldn’t turn down the ‘dream’ job of Manchester United head coach.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

According to recent reports, ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he remarked. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

The 54-year-old Argentine revealed that United first made contact on Sunday after the 4-4 draw in Carrick’s final game left the club in the relegation zone.

‘I never mentioned I wanted to go back in the Premier League,’ said Pochettino, whose first game in charge of United will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

‘All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear. There was some contact. When things became bigger, they are very sensitive.

Sources indicate that ‘We were very transparent with the federation and they understand the situation. The decision between US Soccer and Man United to agree to continue for these two games will not change our commitment.

‘That decision was between the three parties but, of course if Man United agreed different terms, I need to respect that.’.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

According to recent reports, city will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a fresh City, different personnel and even a new look.

Recent findings suggest that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

In a recent development, “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a newly introduced team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

It has been revealed that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

It has been revealed that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca stated. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

In a recent development, by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

In a recent development, diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

It has been revealed that “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the major stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

Recent findings suggest that for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

It has been revealed that “I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

Recent findings suggest that enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

Sources indicate that A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

In a recent development, that is a major chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

It has been revealed that manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

It has been revealed that A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

According to recent reports, enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Industry observers note that porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

In a recent development, just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee says the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

According to recent reports, D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

In a recent development, it is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

In a recent development, A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

According to recent reports, in probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

In a recent development, veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

With it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

According to recent reports, enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

In a recent development, “It is a hard place to come [Porto],” noted Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

Sources indicate that “We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

It has been revealed that porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

Sources indicate that (ANSA) - MILANO, 19 NOV - "Per chi ama il calcio è stata una grande emozione, Ronaldinho è l'essenza del calcio, è un piacere solo stare insieme a lui, ti trasmette la gioia di vivere e di fare calcio, è un bambino per tutta la vita e giocherà a calcio tutta la vita". Lo dice il vicepresidente del Ravenna, Ariedo Braida, sull'esordio di Ronaldinho, domenica contro il Forlì. Braida, evitando di sbilanciarsi sulle elezioni federali del 14 dicembre tra Galliani e Malagò ("il voto è segreto, vinca il migliore"), non conferma se il fuoriclasse brasiliano, 46 anni, tornerà in campo: "Per noi è stata un'emozione, un piacere e un onore. Gianfranco Zola, a margine dell'evento a Sky 'Serie C Next Step', si dice "sorpreso" per il ritorno in campo di Ronaldinho ma sottolinea che "la mission della Serie C è un'altra": "Ronaldinho è uno di quei giocatori che ha ispirato milioni di giovani. In questo senso siamo contenti che li continui ad ispirare. È una fase delicata per il Catanzaro, chiamato a ritrovare compattezza e unità d'intenti per affrontare le difficoltà del momento. Dopo la decisione della società di abbassare i prezzi dei biglietti per le prossime due partite, è arrivato anche l'appello della Curva Massimo Capraro, che attraverso i social ha invitato tutta la tifoseria a mobilitarsi in vista del prossimo impegno contro il Palermo, capolista e avversario atteso al "Ceravolo".

Sources indicate that il cuore del tifo giallorosso ha chiesto alla piazza di restare al fianco della squadra di Mignani, sottolineando quanto sia importante il sostegno dei tifosi proprio in un momento complicato della stagione. L'obiettivo è trasformare lo stadio in una spinta per i giocatori, chiamati a reagire alle difficoltà e a lottare per la maglia.

Industry observers note that nella nota ufficiale della Curva Massimo Capraro si legge: “Il momento è difficile, la classifica brucia, ma è proprio adesso che si vede la stoffa di una vera tifoseria. Non servono calcoli né alibi: sabato tutti al “Ceravolo” a sostenere la maglia. È il momento di risvegliare l’amore viscerale per i nostri colori e dimostrare chi siamo quando la strada si fa in salita. La salvezza e l’orgoglio di Catanzaro passano da qui. Tutti allo stadio con un vessillo giallorosso, coloriamo il ‘Ceravolo’. Avanti Catanzaro”.

Lo spagnolo cerca spazio sulla fascia sinistra: Gattuso potrà valutarlo anche nelle gare con Torino e Atalanta.

Industry observers note that alfonso Pedraza avrà una chance sulla fascia sinistra della Lazio contro il Lecce, approfittando dello stop di Nuno Tavares. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Lo spagnolo cerca spazio dopo un avvio difficile: le gare con i salentini, il Torino e l’Atalanta sono tre occasioni per convincere Rino Gattuso, che finora non si è fidato completamente di lui.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that l’obiettivo non è scavalcare Tavares nelle gerarchie, ma guadagnare la fiducia del tecnico e più minuti, anche a partita in corso. Belahyane ha già saputo sfruttare i problemi di Rovella; ora Pedraza può provare a fare altrettanto durante l’assenza del portoghese.

Le due presenze da titolare di Pedraza risalgono entrambe ad agosto. La prima, contro il Mantova in Coppa Italia, è coincisa con il punto più basso della stagione biancoceleste. La seconda è arrivata a Bologna, all’esordio in campionato: in quel caso il risultato è stato diverso grazie a Davide Frattesi.

It has been revealed that L’esperienza dello spagnolo a Formello non è dunque cominciata nel modo sperato. Nei 251 minuti giocati in Serie A, però, Pedraza ha servito due assist decisivi: il primo contro il Monza, dopo un buon inserimento, e il secondo contro il Genoa, apparso meno cercato. Entrambi hanno mandato a segno Andrea Pinamonti.

Pinamonti sarà titolare anche sabato pomeriggio all’Olimpico contro il Lecce. La Lazio ha costruito soprattutto a sinistra molte occasioni nel corso della stagione, grazie a Tavares e Zaccagni, ma ora deve fare a meno di entrambi i titolari di quella zona del campo.

Industry observers note that davanti a Pedraza ci sarà Noslin: i due dovranno trovare le giuste misure, almeno nei primi minuti. Per lo spagnolo sarà anche l’occasione di avvicinarsi al rendimento mostrato al Villarreal, dove ha costruito la propria carriera dimostrando di poter giocare a certi livelli.

In a recent development, pedraza è tra i pochi nuovi acquisti che non sono ancora entrati nelle grazie dei tifosi. In precedenza, le voci su una possibile partenza di Tavares avevano fatto pensare che potesse diventare lui il titolare. Il portoghese è rimasto e ha mostrato un rendimento diverso rispetto agli anni passati, pur dovendo fare i conti ancora con un infortunio.
