SCOTLAND 2 NORTH MACEDONIA 1: John McGinn at the double to spare the blushes of Pocognoli's shaky Scots on skipper Robertson's substantial night

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:11 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • On the night when the nation looked over its shoulder and celebrated the past, the here and now for Scotland looked distinctly uncertain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:11 EST, 13 November 2026.

On the night when the nation looked over its shoulder and celebrated the past, the here and now for Scotland looked distinctly uncertain.

Coming 40 years and a day after his friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish, pulled on a Scotland jersey for the 102nd and final time, Andy Robertson joined the great man on a mark which, for years, seemed beyond the reach of mere mortals.

Recent findings suggest that by time up, history had mercifully repeated itself at Hampden. Back in the day, Dalglish, by then player-manager at Anfield, sailed into the international sunset on the back of a routine 3-0 win over Luxembourg.

Facing another opponent of modest ability, Robertson’s red letter day didn’t go quite as smoothly. Yet, when the Tottenham man is old and grey and reflecting on the night he created history, the annals will at least record a slender victory.

While his side did just about enough to prevail here, this was another fraught night for Sebastien Pocognoli.

It has been revealed that you can talk about the need for patience under the new manager until the cows come home. But North Macedonia are 71st in FIFA’s rankings. Scotland are 43rd.

John McGinn celebrates in trademark fashion after netting Scotland's winner from the spot.

At Hampden Park, in front of an expectant crowd, Scotland should be putting them to the sword with something to spare.

In a recent development, yet, for long enough, the Belgian’s latest-look side were flat, predictable and plodding. It stated much that it took the intervention of VAR for them to get the penalty which would ultimately lead to three points being accrued.

John McGinn’s second half double saved the Belgian’s blushes and truthfully there was little else to get the Tartan Army off their seats.

In a recent development, too many big-name players scarcely merited pass marks. Too few looked comfortable in the system the manager is trying to bed in.

Sources indicate that if it was a step in the right direction, it was a small one. After five games under the affable Belgian, the progress has certainly not been startling.

While it goes without saying that beating the Swiss in St Gallen on Monday will be an inordinately tougher task, having some hope of moving up a place and securing a kinder draw for the Euros is still better than no hope.

Regardless of what pot they end up in when the draw is made in Belfast next month, a radical improvement will certainly be required across the board if they are to stand any chance of qualifying for the tournament via the front door.

As well as the achievements of Robertson and Dalglish, the career of Craig Gordon was acknowledged before the match with the 84-times capped keeper deservedly afforded a warm hand by the Tartan Army.

McGinn slots home his penalty after Ben Gannon-Doak had been brought down in the area.

Recent findings suggest that there were absolutely no excuses for Scotland here. North Macedonia were a tier-two team in name only. They arrived at Hampden having not won in 12 matches and not scored in eight.

Recent findings suggest that another Pocognoli game saw another back-three combination. This time Luke Graham was selected in the centre of the unit with Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney deployed either side of the Stoke man in what were their first appearances under the Belgian.

It has been revealed that robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak were tasked with providing the width in the 3-4-3. Scott McTominay slotted back into an advanced role beside John McGinn with the returning Che Adams asked to lead the line.

For all there was a healthy crowd in excess of 40,000 inside Hampden, the atmosphere was subdued. In the four Nations League games to date under the new manager, the side hadn’t exactly given the supporters much to feed off.

In a recent development, despite some major guns returning, Scotland made a laboured start to their night’s work. It mentioned much that Graham, on his second appearance, was busier than any defender in white.

Recent findings suggest that the first opening came as a result of an opposition error. John McGinn found Billy Gilmour who fed the overlapping Robertson. The skipper’s cross was well out of Adams’ reach.

Sebastien Pocognoli got his first Hampden win as Scotland boss but it was a nervy night.

It has been revealed that although Ljupche Doriev worried Angus Gunn with a curling effort, Scotland began to exert some degree of control on the match. Lewis Ferguson kept the visitors hemmed in with a header into McTominay’s feet. The Napoli man saw his shot on the spin well saved by Stole Dimitrievski.

Pocognoli was frustrated when Slovakian referee Michal Ocenas blew for a foul on McTominay, his justifiable gripe being that playing an advantage would have seen Robertson have a crack at goal.

Industry observers note that dimitrievski had a decent night. Although Adams’ flashing header from McGinn’s corner took a deflection, a reflex save at his near post added to Scotland’s frustration.

North Macedonia were a spirited but ordinary side. They still had enough to thwart Pocognoli’s men.

Industry observers note that gannon-Doak saw plenty of the ball down the right, yet the end product often wasn’t there. The Bournemouth man did tee up Billy Gilmour for one dangerous cross. McTominay tried to replicate his iconic overhead kick against Denmark nearly a year ago. This time, his aim wasn’t true.

You could hardly blame Pocognoli’s star man for failing to find the net on that occasion.

Scott McTominay attempts an overhead spectacular a year on from THAT goal at Hampden.

That wasn’t the case a few moments later when Adams slipped him in. Dimitrievski saved McTominay’s strike with an outstretched leg when he should have been picking the ball out of his net.

Adams had just blazed a strike high over the top while one-on-one with the keeper although the offside flag saved his blushes.

Industry observers note that the visitors came closer to edging ahead when Eljif Elmas played the pass of the match over Scotland’s static defence to pick out Ezgjan Alioski. His lay-off was smashed into the side net by Enis Bardhi.

Industry observers note that A wholly uninspiring first-half concluded with Robertson advancing up the left and launching a cross halfway to Castlemilk. This was not going well.

Pocognoli waited on the edge of the pitch for his players returning, his enthusiastic applause clearly audible in the arena.

Sources indicate that his hopes of a breakthrough at the outset of the second period were dashed in extraordinary fashion. Adams did well to chase a ball down to the line and cut it back. McTominay and his marker couldn’t connect, leaving Gilmour the simple task of firing into an unguarded net. Leaning back, his failure to even hit the target was unfathomable.

Elmin Rastoder celebrates after silencing Hampden with a leveller for North Macedonia.

Within seconds, the sense of relief inside Hampden was palpable as the opener finally arrived. Porteous got enough distance on his clearing header for Adams to barge Visar Musliu out of the way.

McGinn was alert to the situation and burst into the box. His crisp strike finally had the beating of the goalkeeper.

Recent findings suggest that it should have settled Pocognoli’s side and paved the way for a comfortable result. Instead, they were pegged back within three minutes.

It was all just so simple and so avoidable. Bardhi’s whipped corner only needed McTominay to outjump his man. Flat-footed as the delivery arrived, he could only watch on in horror as Elmin Rastoder’s flashing header beat Angus Gunn.

Although Gilmour worked the keeper with a low strike, North Macedonia also sniffed a second goal. Time and time again, they got into pockets of space on the flanks and fired in dangerous crosses.

Industry observers note that adams made way for Oli McBurnie, the Hull man desperately hoping for his first goal on his 21st international appearance. He had a gilt-edged chance to get off the mark when rolled in by McGinn, but selflessly passed to the overlapping Gannon-Doak.

Scotland move on to their final game away in Switzerland as they look to finish on a high note.

The winger appeared to take a heavy touch which allowed the keeper to rescue the situation. VAR, however, spotted that Dimitrievski had impeded him. Penalty.

McGinn did the necessary from 12 yards, smashing the ball straight down the middle for his 24th international goal.

Industry observers note that north Macedonia, to their credit, kept going for it. They sensed a fragility in Scotland. Everyone in the ground could.

Sources indicate that mcGinn’s calm conversion proved to be just about enough to get the job done. But it’s fair to suggest that we are still awaiting lift-off in the new era.

SCOTLAND (3-4-1-2): Gunn; Porteous, Graham, Tierney; Gannon-Doak (Hickey 76), Ferguson, Gilmour (Christie 76), Robertson; McGinn; Adams (McBurnie 67), McTominay. Booked: Ferguson. Manager: Sebastien Pocognoli.

NORTH MACEDONIA (4-2-3-1): Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Mladenovski, Musliu, Alioski; Gashtarov (Elezi 64), Elmas (Stankovski 78); Churlinov (Maleski 64), Bardhi, Doriev (Nikolov 85); Rastoder. Booked: None. Manager: Goce Sedloski.

Referee: Michal Ocenas (Slovakia).

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l’ex portiere dice: «Lo strapotere dell’Inter mi sembra evidente, per progetto e per forza degli interpreti. CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Reina distingue così la forza dell’Inter dalla situazione delle altre formazioni citate.

According to recent reports, reina parla anche della classifica e dei due allenatori a cui è legato: «La Lazio è prima, il Como è quinto e su quelle panchine ci sono due miei amici che vedo e sento spesso. Diventerà una guida per la categoria.» Sul paragone con Guardiola aggiunge: «Il Guardiola 3.0? Pep ha visto cose che altri non riuscivano a vedere, ha inventato, ha vinto e stravinto, ha conquistato. E Cesc lo ricorda».

Tech Report: Inside Boreham Wood, the only unbeaten team in England's top seven tiers: Boss LUKE GARRARD explains how play-off heartache and a 'genius' owner are fuelling his swashbuckling side's promotion bid

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.
  • Boreham Wood are on their own crusade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026.

Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.

Boreham Wood are on their own crusade. And the Holy Grail is a long-coveted place in the EFL for the runaway leaders of the National League. They have 44 points from 16 games with 44 goals and are 12 points clear ahead of a trip to Yeovil on Saturday, finding success with a distinct passing style.

In a remarkable 4-3 comeback win against Hartlepool earlier this month, Luke Garrard's team made 1,022 passes, beating the Premier League record of 1,015 set by Manchester City against Swansea in April 2018.

The electric start to this campaign is, according to Garrard, fuelled by the lingering pain of defeat in the play-off final at Wembley in May when they conceded an equaliser in the seventh minute of stoppage time and lost on penalties.

According to recent reports, 'That broke me mentally for four or five days,' the Wood boss tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I reflected hugely and had a long, hard look at myself because I could not walk back for the first day of pre-season without the energy and heart for the job.

'I spoke to the owners and the staff about the first meeting I wanted to have when we came back in. It involved everyone at the club, and it was a message to tell all of them that as much as it hurt us, we needed to use the hurt as our fuel and our driving force.

'We got quite lucky getting some results on the board quite rapidly and that builds momentum and belief.'.

National League leaders Boreham Wood, under the guidance of their manager Luke Garrard, are the last unbeaten team in the top seven tiers of English football.

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500. They share Meadow Park with Arsenal Women and Arsenal Under 21s and U18s.

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500 by chairman Danny Hunter and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director and in charge of recruitment strategy. They are punching above their weight with a mid-table budget.

Hunter senior is a former props master in the film industry who worked at the nearby Elstree Studios among others, and whose father Mickey was a double promotion winning manager of club in the 1970s.

He took control in 1999 and has overseen investment of more than £14million and the rise from the depths of the Isthmian League to the brink of the EFL, forging effective relationships with local authorities and Premier League neighbours Arsenal, who use Meadow Park for their Women, Under-21 and Under-18 teams.

Arsenal ad boards surround an immaculate pitch, and work is underway at the venue on a £4m project to create a covered South Stand terrace incorporating improved 'Fan Zone' style facilities for away fans and a upcoming first-team building.

Garrard's team train in the mornings on the artificial pitches beside the stadium, which are available for community use in the evenings and home in the afternoons to the club's academy.

Manchester City's Iliman Ndiaye and Hull's Sorba Thomas were both nurtured as young players at Boreham Wood. So was Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024 and sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5m in August.

The Abdulmalik fee shattered the non-League record set when Fleetwood Town sold Jamie Vardy to Leicester in 2012.

Sources indicate that there was an untidy episode towards the end of the transfer window when Abdulmalik went public to plead for a move, but the Hunters secured an enviable price for their star and in another example of their good housekeeping have yet to reinvest the money in the team. It is still there as a war chest as they target promotion.

Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024, was sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5million in August.

According to recent reports, the club is run by chairman Danny Hunter (pictured) and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director. Hunter Snr is a former props master in the film industry.

The windfall from Wood's famous FA Cup run in 2021-22 was invested into refitting the interiors of the ground including the dressing rooms and swish hospitality areas recognised among the best in non-League.

Meadow Park has a bar bedecked with souvenirs from those games and named in honour of Mark Ricketts, scorer of the goal to beat Bournemouth, who were at the time bound for promotion to the Premier League, and which clinched a date with Everton in the fifth round at Goodison Park.

'At no stage has the chairman given me any pressure to generate money from prize funds and cup runs,' claims 41-year-old Garrard. 'It's only ever been about creating moments and memories.

'He (Hunter) is a Boreham Wood boy through and through and it's always been his greatest wish to lead the club into the EFL. He wants to leave a legacy. I adore him, I think he's a genius. We have a great working relationship. I do not take for granted the luxury of being manager here, especially after losing my job two years ago.'.

Garrard has a long association with the club. First as a player, briefly in 2005 and then returning for a second spell four years later, a loan move from Wimbledon which became permanent and led him into his first coaching roles and the manager's job.

It has been revealed that he took control in 2015 with the Wood in the top tier of non-League for the first time. Three times they reached the play-offs without promotion and there were many highs including Goodison before Garrard's tearful exit after relegation in April 2024, only for him to be back in charge by September.

It has been revealed that during five months away, he turned down interest from one club because it took him too far from his family home and received two direct and sobering rejections from National League clubs. Feedback from the first told him he 'wasn't on the list and never would be' and from the second that he 'wasn't good enough' for them.

Perhaps it reveals some of football's inherent petty-mindedness towards Boreham Wood. They are perceived by some as upstarts with limited history and small crowds, putting the noses of 'bigger' clubs out of joint with the streamlined success of their business model and Hunter's backing, like a non-League version of Bournemouth or Brentford.

They have been known to charge scouts for tickets and charge away teams to broadcast, which some refuse to do on a point of principle. For a time, they had a reputation for pragmatic and unattractive football – but not any longer.

Garrard was rejected by two National League clubs and found himself back at Boreham Wood. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it.

Prolific striker Matt Rush has is fuelling Boreham Wood's promotion push.

Industry observers note that garrard was probably entitled to have expected more interest in his services. Instead, he spent two days following the second of those rejections in earnest conversation with his wife about the need to look for work away from football when out of the blue came a call from Boreham Wood.

Industry observers note that within another two days he was back in his old job. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it. 'It was the best team in the National South with the best players, the best facilities and the best budget. I had to go and deliver.'.

Recent findings suggest that and he did. With promotion back to the National League at the first attempt. Then the near-miss heartache of Wembley. Now this early-season surge thanks in part to the goals of striker Matt Rush. The Wood seem to have emerged stronger despite selling their most talented individual, which is a reassuring situation for any coach.

Unbeaten since April in the National League, they scored 25 goals in seven games in October and League One Wigan became the first team to beat them in any competition this season, in the FA Cup first round on Saturday.

It could yet prove a blessing in Boreham Wood's quest for the Holy Grail.

Industry News: Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under latest head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • In a recent development, so, earn it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under latest head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a latest contract.

In a recent development, so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face noted it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

In a recent development, mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

In a recent development, mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ newly introduced head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

According to recent reports, for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A massive European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola mentioned, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

In a recent development, as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

Industry observers note that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It has been revealed that it owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Sources indicate that atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

Andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

So far, four of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season have played on this opening matchday and all four have won:.

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

"We can achieve everything we want." 💪Dominik Szoboszlai full of belief after Liverpool's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid 👀🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ebSvagW4yx.

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ.

According to recent reports, first Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

In a recent development, liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

According to recent reports, the Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed latest contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a newly introduced contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

Sources indicate that “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

It has been revealed that former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

According to recent reports, the Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. Industry observers note that when Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

Sources indicate that “This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

In a recent development, andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

Industry observers note that “I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola remarked. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

Industry observers note that “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Atletico Madrid at the moment sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

Sources indicate that “We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Luis Figo continua a essere molto legato al Real Madrid.
  • It has been revealed that L'ex stella di Real Madrid e Barcellona ha poi elogiato Yan Diomande, protagonista di una crescita importante nella squadra di José Mourinho.
  • Parole positive anche per Arda Guler, definito un elemento "importante nella costruzione del gioco grazie alla sua tecnica e alla capacità di dare continuità alle proprie prestazioni".

Luis Figo continua a essere molto legato al Real Madrid. L'ex campione portoghese, oggi ambasciatore di Betfair, ha parlato del momento dei Blancos soffermandosi soprattutto sulla situazione di Vinicius Junior, reduce da un periodo meno brillante rispetto ai suoi standard. Per il Pallone d'Oro 2000, però, il brasiliano non ha perso qualità e presto tornerà ai suoi livelli abituali: "Vinicius è un giocatore che tornerà al suo livello, al suo status, per la qualità che possiede", ha spiegato Figo, ricordando come anche i migliori calciatori attraversino momenti difficili. "È normale che le prestazioni possano risentirne. Tutti i grandi giocatori possono vivere periodi in cui non sono al massimo, ma questo non ha nulla a che vedere con il loro valore".

It has been revealed that L'ex stella di Real Madrid e Barcellona ha poi elogiato Yan Diomande, protagonista di una crescita importante nella squadra di José Mourinho. "Ha saputo sfruttare le opportunità e si è adattato gradualmente a un club esigente come il Real Madrid. È un giocatore che può cambiare le partite: è veloce, vede la porta e crea pericoli". Secondo Figo, una delle qualità più importanti dell'esterno è anche la disponibilità in fase difensiva: "Forse non sembra il giocatore tecnicamente più raffinato, ma attacca la profondità e ha una caratteristica fondamentale per chi gioca nel Real: contribuisce anche senza palla".

Parole positive anche per Arda Guler, definito un elemento "importante nella costruzione del gioco grazie alla sua tecnica e alla capacità di dare continuità alle proprie prestazioni".

Figo ha infine riconosciuto il ruolo di José Mourinho nella nuova fase del Real Madrid. Secondo il portoghese, il tecnico ha inciso sulle scelte tattiche e sull'equilibrio della squadra: "Non c'è dubbio che il merito sia suo. I cambiamenti fatti hanno portato risultati positivi. Alcuni giocatori sono stati spostati e la squadra ha guadagnato solidità, sia nel pressing sia nella fase difensiva". Proprio l'attenzione maggiore al lavoro senza palla sarebbe, secondo Figo, la chiave della crescita dei Blancos: "Con la qualità che hanno, hanno sempre avuto la capacità di creare occasioni e segnare. Quando aggiungi equilibrio difensivo e concedi meno opportunità agli avversari, si spiega perché il Real sta vivendo questo momento positivo".

In un'intervista concessa al podcast serbo Ss Calcio, il difensore del Milan Pavlovic ha parlato della sua esperienza rossonera e ha risposto anche ad una domanda sugli avversari più tosti affrontati in Serie A.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

«Conceiçao ha bandito la Nutella e da allora non ce l’hanno più concessa. È un bravo ragazzo, mi piace, ma aveva dei metodi duri, 'alla Hitler'. Tre giorni prima di una partita, alcuni calciatori sono andati ad un concerto fino alle 23. Aveva degli assistenti, o delle spie, che gli facevano rapporto, e ne ha fatto un tale circo che nella partita successiva a nessuno di quei cinque o sei giocatori è stato permesso di scendere in campo», ha detto a proposito dell'ex allenatore del Milan.

Quando gli hanno chiesto degli avversari che lo hanno messo più in difficoltà quando li ha affrontati ha detto: «L'avversario contro cui ho faticato di più fisicamente è stato sicuramente Romelu Lukaku. C'è anche Marcus Thuram. È forte, veloce e molto abile con la palla. Contro Lautaro bisogna stare molto attenti in area di rigore. Se non lo si marca stretto, segna. Non si può lasciargli spazio».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L'ex arbitro Graziano Cesari, su SportMediaset, ha parlato della linea Orsato e di come sta andando l'esperienza degli arbitri in questo campionato. Questo è quanto ha sottolineato l'ex direttore di gara:.

-I pro e i contro della nuova linea arbitrale?

Recent findings suggest that mi convince molto il decisionismo, è l'arbitro che decide sul terreno di gioco. Mi convince il tempo effettivo di gioco, i gialli in calo, i rossi, pensa solo ai rigori. Da questo punto di vista mi convince. Ma non mi convince quello che fa sempre discutere, su falli di mano e interpretazione e quando il VAR deve intervenire oppure no. Non abbiamo ancora una spiegazione chiara.

-Molti degli errori arrivano dal VAR?

Sources indicate that sì. Non mi sono piaciuti gli interventi del VAR e non vorrei che i varisti vogliano superare in qualche modo l'arbitro che per Orsato è quello che in realtà comanda. Ma mi sembra che ci sia qualcuno che abbia preso questo ruolo davanti ai monitor a Lissone. Magari non sono riusciti a raggiungere livelli eccelsi da arbitri e tendono a mettersi in evidenza.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

-La follia più grande di questa stagione e quella che ritieni la follia più grande nel calcio?

It has been revealed that la mia è stata espellere Van Basten quando non aveva fatto niente. Una grande follia e da lì ho coniato il termine, su me stesso, 'sei un folle'. Quest'anno ce ne sono state tantissime e mi riferisco all'ultima, in Bologna-Parma, con l'espulsione del calciatore gialloblù. Quando non ti fanno vedere tutte le immagini selezionate che sono in sala a Lissone te ne fanno vedere una parte. Perché vuoi mettere in difficoltà il direttore di gara?

-Chi sono i migliori quest'anno?

Recent findings suggest that mi sono piaciuti Massa e Guida. In questo momento ho dubbi che la classe arbitrale sia tra le migliori. Perché per me quella inglese è una classe arbitrale molto forte. Anche per la forma di arbitraggio che è professionismo, forse servirebbe questo in Italia.

#49759. Breaking: Andy's substantial night should have been so much more straightforward but that won't matter when he reflects on history made at Hampden

Breaking: Andy's substantial night should have been so much more straightforward but that won't matter when he reflects on history made at Hampden

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (833 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:21 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:24 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Industry observers note that if Andy Robertson’s first 101 caps for Scotland taught him anything, it’s that we have never been a nation to make life easy for ourselves.
  • Why, therefore, would he have expected cap No102 to be any different?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:21 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:24 EST, 13 November 2026.

Industry observers note that if Andy Robertson’s first 101 caps for Scotland taught him anything, it’s that we have never been a nation to make life easy for ourselves. It’s in our DNA.

Why, therefore, would he have expected cap No102 to be any different?

This was meant to have been a celebration of one of Scotland’s greatest-ever servants on the night when he equalled Kenny Dalglish’s total appearances against the whipping boys of Nations League Group B1.

Sources indicate that as the cliché goes, there’s no gimmes at this level. But that’s nonsense. This is exactly what Robertson’s special night should have been. A gimme.

The visitors hadn’t registered a goal yet in this campaign, never mind a point. They were rotten when Robertson and Co scored twice without reply in Skopje last month, and it was the same story for much of this forgettable contest.

The problem is that Scotland weren’t much better. In the first half, at least.

Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps as Scotland saw off North Macedonia.

Thankfully, they got the job done after the break to ensure it would be a night Robertson will look back on fondly after all.

He’s earned that too, even if his own individual performance didn’t quite hit the heights of so many that have gone before. But nobody will remember that.

According to recent reports, perhaps he knackered himself by covering what must have been around 10km in a small-sided kickabout during the warm-up. He may not have the same turn of pace in his arsenal that he possessed when he first broke into the international fold as a fresh-faced teenager. But, in terms of intensity, the 32-year-old is still an animal, in the nicest possible way. He hassled and harried every one of his team-mates throughout the pre-game stuff, barking out all sorts of instructions along the way.

In a recent development, in many ways, he is still the same standard-bearer he’s always been. It was a shame he couldn’t quite lead the way when the serious stuff got started.

Recent findings suggest that operating on the left-hand side of a four-man midfield, the Spurs man – as he does as frequently as ever – bombed up and down the flank all night. However, his deliveries from several promising positions weren’t quite up to scratch.

A couple hit the first man. A couple cleared the upright. None caused any sort of alarm in the North Macedonian backline.

Robertson was his customary energetic self as he bombed up and down the left-hand side.

He was made to work harder than he would have liked at the other end too, as the visitors threatened to spoil the party on more than one occasion in the second 45.

Industry observers note that in truth, he didn’t look particularly comfortable in Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest-look side. Then again, few did.

Recent findings suggest that the Belgian will be given plenty of time to really put his stamp on this Scotland team, but there’s no two ways about it. The early signs are uninspiring to say the least.

By the end, people got sick of the attritional style employed by Steve Clarke. Pocognoli arrived with a reputation for going with a more enterprising approach.

In a recent development, really? It’s fair to say, the wait to see it in action goes on.

Sources indicate that it’s not the time to panic. But you get the sense patience is already being stretched amongst some sections of the Tartan Army.

They weren’t shy in airing their frustrations last night. Scott McTominay was on the receiving end of a few grumbles, as was Ben Gannon-Doak who once again did so much right until the all-vital crucial last bit.

Yes, he may have won the winning penalty which John McGinn duly slotted away, but let’s be honest, there was more than a touch of good fortune about it.

The Scotland skipper leads his side out at Hampden on a night he will remember forever.

He should have burst the net when put clean through by Oli McBurnie long before keeper Stole Dimitrievski caught him near the byline.

According to recent reports, the Bournemouth youngster is seen by many as undroppable, and there’s merit to that argument in that Pocognoli doesn’t have anyone else like him to call upon. However, he needs to improve the final part of his game to ensure he becomes Scotland’s main man in the years to come.

Had Scotland been a few goals to the good by the time McGinn stepped up to notch his second of the night, you suspect Robertson may have fancied taking the spot-kick himself.

If only it had been that comfortable.

Still, the record books will show that Robertson’s record-equalling night will ultimately go down as a triumph for all involved, even if it didn’t feel like it at the time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that terminata la seconda pausa nazionali è tempo di tornare a pensare alla Serie A. Domenica pomeriggio infatti, alle ore 18:00, i rossoneri ospiteranno i laziali del Frosinone, squadra allenata da Alvini che, nonostante l’ultima sconfitta in campionato contro il Cagliari per 1-0, si trova al 6° posto in classifica a soli 4 punti dal Diavolo.

Nella storia sono stati pochi gli incontri tra le due squadre, solo sei. La prima in assoluto fu quella del 20/12/2015 quando i rossoneri vinsero in rimonta 4-2 con le reti di Alex, Bacca, Abate e Bonaventura. Domenica a Milano San Siro ci sarà il settimo match ufficiale tra le due squadre. Di seguito tutti i precedenti.

20/12/2015 Frosinone - Milan 2-4.

01/05/2016 Milan - Frosinone 3-3.

26/12/2018 Frosinone - Milan 0-0.

19/05/2019 Milan - Frosinone 2-0.

02/12/2023 Milan - Frosinone 3-1.

03/02/2024 Frosinone - Milan 2-3.

Intervistato durante il podcast Passa dal BSMT di Gianluca Gazzoli, l'ex difensore Daniele Adani ha parlato anche del rapporto con l'amico Antonio Cassano e chiuso definitivamente le porte a un possibile ritorno della Bobo Tv. Di seguito la risposta dell'opinionista attualmente a Rai Sport.

Industry observers note that sul rapporto con Cassano: "Antonio c'è sempre, ma sente l'esigenza di essere coinvolto. Io gli dico sempre: 'Sei l'unica persona a cui concedo tutto'. Per la lealtà, la passione, la faccia che mi dimostra che è sempre quella. Anche in alcune gestioni che a volte sono totalmente assurde. Lui si butta nel fuoco per te anche se la pensa diversamente da te. Lui dice sempre che chi lo comprende di più di tutti siamo io e sua moglie Carolina. Io lo faccio col cuore, mi viene naturale".

No secco a un possibile ritorno della Bobo Tv: "Fino al momento della rottura comunque la ricordo e sono grato di averla vissuta. Sono quasi contento che si sia fermato. Meglio così. Ritorno? Dal mio punto di vista, credo che neanche se ne parlerà, è una cosa archiviata per sempre".

According to recent reports, su Vieri: "Auguro il meglio io, non si vive di rancore per com'è andata. Senza portare rancore, ma con la fermezza e la consapevolezza che non ci sarà più quel tempo".

It has been revealed that E’ andato in scena la prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, riconoscimento dedicato alle figure che hanno lasciato il segno nel panorama calcistico nazionale. Tra i vincitori figura anche il vicepresidente della SSC Napoli, Edoardo De Laurentiis, premiato per i meriti conseguiti nell’area della Governance: “E’ per me un grande onore ricevere questo riconoscimento, ma la gioia è doppia per averlo condiviso con mio padre, che è il mio mentore e la mia guida. Ho mosso i primi passi in questo mondo quando ero ancora molto giovane, ho commesso diversi sbagli, ma mi impegno quotidiano per crescere ed essere all’altezza del mio ruolo”.

In a recent development, successivamente, a margine della cerimonia di premiazione, il vicepresidente ha aggiunto: “La chiave è proseguire giorno dopo giorno con costanza, facendo gruppo. La coesione è fondamentale per raggiungere gli obiettivi prefissati. Diventerà la futura casa del Napoli (riferendosi al nuovo centro sportivo), un luogo in cui far crescere i giovani, costruire il nostro vivaio e scoprire nuovi talenti. Abbiamo vissuto tantissime esperienze entusiasmanti, dall’era Spalletti fino a Conte. La più grande è stata osservare la squadra capace di conquistare costantemente traguardi prestigiosi e di mantenersi sempre ad altissimi livelli”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il ritorno di Ronaldinho sul terreno di gioco, a oltre dieci anni dall'ultima apparizione, ha rappresentato un momento speciale per il calcio. Domenica 15 novembre, in occasione del derby tra Ravenna e Forlì, il brasiliano è tornato a giocare, attirando l'attenzione anche fuori dai confini della Serie C. Un evento che ha lasciato il segno e sul quale si sono soffermati Ariedo Braida e Gianfranco Zola, intervenuti a margine di "Serie C Next Stop", a Milano.

Il vicepresidente del Ravenna, Ariedo Braida, ha sottolineato soprattutto la gioia e l'entusiasmo che il fuoriclasse brasiliano riesce ancora a trasmettere, definendo il suo ritorno un momento indimenticabile per chi ama questo sport.

"Per chi ama il calcio è una grande emozione. Ronaldinho è l'essenza del calcio ed è un piacere solo stare assieme a lui perché ti trasmette la gioia di vivere e di fare calcio. Lui è un bambino che resterà sempre bambino e giocherà a calcio per tutta la vita. Per noi è stato bellissimo, un'emozione e per un giorno abbiamo catalizzato l'attenzione dei mass media di tutto il mondo e questo è un piacere e un onore per noi e spero anche per tutti quelli che amano il calcio, la nostra categoria, il Ravenna".

Braida ha poi lasciato aperta la possibilità di rivedere Ronaldinho in campo, senza però sbilanciarsi sul futuro: "Lo rivedremo? Questo si vedrà. È prematuro parlarne".

Anche Gianfranco Zola, vicepresidente della Lega Pro, ha commentato il ritorno in campo del brasiliano, riconoscendone il valore e l'impatto avuto su tanti giovani appassionati. L'occasione, però, è stata anche per ribadire la centralità del progetto di valorizzazione dei talenti portato avanti dalla Serie C.

"Sono rimasto sorpreso come credo tanti, ma la mission della C, con rispetto parlando, è sempre la stessa. Ronaldinho ha ispirato milioni di giovani, e siamo contenti che continui a farlo, ma noi vogliamo e dobbiamo creare le condizioni migliori per i nostri ragazzi, affinché possano poi seguire il suo percorso".
